items.q: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: My mom made me cleaning my room.
He let his sister to use his bike.
The new rule lets students choose their own seats.
The new rule lets students to choose their own seats.
The cold weather keeps the milk freshly.
items.exp: let은 「let + 목적어 + 동사원형」으로 쓰므로 lets students choose가 옳아요. 나머지는 to choose, cleaning, freshly(부사), to use처럼 목적격 보어의 형태가 틀려요.
items.passage: At the same time, they let people enjoy the beauty of nature.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 keep과 쓰임이 같은(「keep + 목적어 + 형용사」) 것은?
choices: She always keeps her promises.
Keep going straight for two blocks.
He keeps a dog in the yard.
Please keep the windows open.
I keep a diary every night.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 keep은 '~을 …하게 유지하다'로 목적어(species) 뒤에 형용사(safe)가 와요. keep the windows open도 목적어 뒤에 형용사 open이 와요. 나머지는 keep 뒤에 명사만 있거나 -ing가 와요.
items.passage: They [keep] many animal and plant species safe.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 국립공원은 사람들이 자연을 즐기지 못하도록 출입을 막는 곳이다.
국립공원은 동식물을 보호하면서 사람들이 자연의 아름다움을 즐기게 해 준다.
국립공원은 동물만 보호하고 식물은 보호 대상에 포함하지 않는다.
이어서 소개되는 두 국립공원은 모두 아프리카에 있다.
국립공원은 자연을 개발해 관광지로 바꾸려고 만든 곳이다.
items.exp: 2~3번 문장에서 국립공원은 동식물을 안전하게 지키는 동시에 사람들이 자연을 즐기게 한다고 했어요. 소개되는 공원은 남아메리카와 아프리카에 하나씩 있어요.
items.passage: National parks are special places for preserving nature. They keep many animal and plant species safe. At the same time, they let people enjoy the beauty of nature. Let's take a look at two famous national parks in South America and Africa.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 this가 가리키는 것으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 칠레라는 나라를 여행하는 것
겨울에 빙하를 구경하는 것
야생동물을 가까이에서 만나는 것
하루 동안 사계절을 경험하는 것
하루 종일 눈 속을 걷는 것
items.exp: 앞 문장 'you can experience four seasons in one day'를 받는 말이에요. 따라서 하루에 사계절을 경험하는 것을 뜻해요.
items.passage: Can you believe you can experience four seasons in one day? Torres del Paine National Park in Chile is the perfect place for [this].

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 It과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: I love this song. It is my favorite.
It was snowing heavily last night.
It is a famous park in Chile.
It is important to keep the park clean.
I found my pen, and it was under the desk.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 It은 날씨를 나타내는 비인칭 주어로 '그것'이라고 해석하지 않아요. It was snowing도 날씨의 비인칭 주어예요. 나머지는 앞에 나온 대상을 가리키는 대명사이거나 가주어예요.
items.passage: It is famous for its dynamic weather. [It] can be sunny, rainy, or snowy in a single day!

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 두 It에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것은?
choices: 첫 번째 It은 가주어이고, 두 번째 It은 Chile를 가리킨다.
두 It 모두 Torres del Paine 국립공원을 가리킨다.
두 It 모두 날씨를 나타내는 비인칭 주어이다.
첫 번째 It은 비인칭 주어이고, 두 번째 It은 날씨를 가리키는 대명사이다.
첫 번째 It은 Torres del Paine 국립공원을 가리키고, 두 번째 It은 뜻이 없는 비인칭 주어이다.
items.exp: 7번 문장의 It은 앞 문장의 Torres del Paine 국립공원을 받는 대명사이고, 8번 문장의 It은 날씨를 말할 때 쓰는 비인칭 주어예요.
items.passage: [It] is famous for its dynamic weather. [It] can be sunny, rainy, or snowy in a single day!

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Jeju is one of the most beautiful islands in Korea.
One of my best friend lives in Busan.
She is one of the most famous singers in Asia.
One of the students was late for class.
Seoul is one of the biggest cities in Korea.
items.exp: 「one of the + 최상급 + 복수 명사」, 「one of + 복수 명사」 형태이므로 best friend는 best friends가 되어야 해요.
items.passage: For example, Grey Glacier, [one of the most wonderful glaciers] in Chile, welcomes you in the park.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Grey Glacier는 칠레에서 가장 큰 빙하이다.
하루 안에 맑은 날씨, 비, 눈이 모두 나타날 수 있다.
방문객은 빙하 위를 걸을 수 없고 멀리서 보기만 해야 한다.
이 공원에는 산과 호수는 없고 빙원만 있다.
하루에 사계절을 경험하려면 한 달 이상 머물러야 한다.
items.exp: 8번 문장에서 하루 안에 맑고 비 오고 눈이 올 수 있다고 했어요. Grey Glacier는 '가장 멋진 빙하 중 하나'이고, 산·호수·빙원이 모두 있어요.
items.passage: Can you believe you can experience four seasons in one day? Torres del Paine National Park in Chile is the perfect place for this. It is famous for its dynamic weather. It can be sunny, rainy, or snowy in a single day! Also, you can see mountains, lakes, and even a big ice field in this park. For example, Grey Glacier, one of the most wonderful glaciers in Chile, welcomes you in the park. It is exciting to walk on the glacier and enjoy the icy view.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 It과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: It is Monday, so I have a math test.
It is raining hard in Seoul now.
It is important to drink enough water.
I lost my umbrella, but it is in the bus.
It is about two kilometers to the station.
items.exp: 밑줄 친 It은 to부정사구(to walk ~)를 대신하는 가주어예요. It is important to drink도 같은 구조예요. 나머지는 비인칭 주어(날씨·요일·거리)이거나 대명사예요.
items.passage: [It] is exciting to walk on the glacier and enjoy the icy view.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
강을 따라 자전거를 타는 것은 재미있다.
choices: This is fun that ride a bike along the river.
It fun is to ride a bike along the river.
It is fun to ride a bike along the river.
It is fun to riding a bike along the river.
It is fun ride a bike along the river.
items.exp: 「It(가주어) is + 형용사 + to부정사(진주어)」 구조예요. 나머지는 to가 빠지거나 어순이 틀리거나 to 뒤에 -ing를 썼어요.
items.passage: It is exciting to walk on the glacier and enjoy the icy view.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 making과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: He enjoys swimming in the lake.
My hobby is collecting old coins.
Thank you for visiting us.
She is good at taking pictures.
The students are cleaning the park now.
items.exp: making은 'be동사 + -ing'의 현재진행형이에요. are cleaning도 현재진행형이에요. 나머지는 보어·전치사의 목적어·동사의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사예요.
items.passage: The park is [making] efforts to preserve its natural beauty.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 to enter와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: She has a lot of homework to finish.
I want to visit Chile someday.
My dream is to become a vet.
He saved money to buy a new bike.
It is fun to watch birds.
items.exp: to enter는 '입장하기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법이에요. to buy도 '사기 위해'의 목적이에요. 나머지는 각각 목적어, 보어, 형용사적 용법, 진주어예요.
items.passage: First, it controls the number of visitors, so they should book [to enter] the park.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 it과 they가 가리키는 것을 바르게 짝지은 것은?
choices: it - the glacier / they - visitors
it - the park / they - trails
it - visitors / they - the park
it - the park / they - visitors
it - Chile / they - visitors
items.exp: controls의 주어 it은 문맥상 공원(the park)이에요. 예약해야 하는 they는 앞의 visitors예요.
items.passage: First, [it] controls the number of visitors, so [they] should book to enter the park.

items.q:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
The number of visitors to the park ___ growing every year.
choices: is
are
were
be
have been
items.exp: the number of ~(~의 수)는 단수 취급하므로 단수 동사 is가 와요. a number of ~는 '많은 ~'로 복수 취급해요.
items.passage: First, it controls the number of visitors, so they should book to enter the park.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
많은 방문객들이 그 공원에 왔다.
choices: A number of visitors came to the park.
The number of visitors came to the park.
A number of visitor came to the park.
A number of visitors comes to the park.
Number of visitors came to the park.
items.exp: '많은 ~'는 a number of + 복수 명사로 나타내요. The number of는 '~의 수'라는 뜻이라 문맥에 맞지 않고, 나머지는 단수형 visitor, 동사 comes, 관사 누락으로 틀려요.
items.passage: First, it controls the number of visitors, so they should book to enter the park.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 방문객이 버린 쓰레기는 공원 직원이 모두 치운다.
모든 산책로가 하이킹을 위해 방문객에게 열려 있다.
공원 안 호텔은 플라스틱 제품도 일부 함께 쓴다.
방문객은 예약 없이도 원하는 만큼 입장할 수 있다.
공원 안 호텔에서는 플라스틱을 쓰지 않고 친환경 제품만 쓴다.
items.exp: 16번 문장에서 호텔은 플라스틱을 쓰지 않고 친환경 제품만 쓴다고 했어요. 방문객은 예약해야 하고, 일부 산책로만 열려 있으며, 쓰레기는 방문객이 가져가요.
items.passage: The park is making efforts to preserve its natural beauty. First, it controls the number of visitors, so they should book to enter the park. Second, only some park trails are open to visitors for hiking. Third, the park makes visitors take their trash with them when they leave. There's one more thing: the hotels in the park do not use plastic and only use eco-friendly products.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 makes와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: She made her son a paper plane.
The sad movie made me cry.
My dad made pancakes for us.
They made a plan for the trip.
He made a lot of money last year.
items.exp: makes visitors take는 「make + 목적어 + 동사원형」(~가 …하게 하다)이에요. made me cry도 같은 구조예요. 나머지는 make가 '만들다'로 쓰였어요.
items.passage: Third, the park [makes] visitors take their trash with them when they leave.

items.q:
윗글의 내용을 요약한 문장의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Torres del Paine National Park keeps its nature beautiful by (A) the number of visitors and by using only (B) products in its hotels.
choices: (A) ignoring - (B) dangerous
(A) controlling - (B) eco-friendly
(A) controlling - (B) plastic
(A) increasing - (B) plastic
(A) increasing - (B) eco-friendly
items.exp: 공원은 방문객 수를 조절하고(13번), 호텔에서는 친환경 제품만 쓴다고 했어요(16번).
items.passage: The park is making efforts to preserve its natural beauty. First, it controls the number of visitors, so they should book to enter the park. Second, only some park trails are open to visitors for hiking. Third, the park makes visitors take their trash with them when they leave. There's one more thing: the hotels in the park do not use plastic and only use eco-friendly products.

items.q: 다음 중 병렬 구조가 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: The hotel does not sell plastic bags and only selling paper bags.
The hotel does not sell plastic bags and only sold paper bags.
The hotel does not sell plastic bags and only sells paper bags.
The hotel does not sell plastic bags and only sell paper bags.
The hotel does not sell plastic bags and only to sell paper bags.
items.exp: and 앞뒤의 동사는 같은 형태여야 해요. 주어가 The hotel(3인칭 단수)이므로 does not sell과 only sells가 병렬돼요.
items.passage: There's one more thing: the hotels in the park do not use plastic and only use eco-friendly products.

items.q: 윗글의 첫 문장에 대한 응답으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: No, I wasn't. What are they?
No, I don't. What are they?
Yes, I did. What are they?
Yes, I heard. What are they?
No, I haven't. What are they?
items.exp: Have you heard ~?는 현재완료 의문문이므로 have/haven't로 답해요. Yes/No와 시제가 맞는 것은 No, I haven't.뿐이에요.
items.passage: Have you heard about the Big Five? They are lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and buffaloes.

items.q: 윗글에서 Big Five에 포함되지 않는 동물은?
choices: leopards
buffaloes
lions
elephants
giraffes
items.exp: Big Five는 lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, buffaloes예요. giraffes는 언급되지 않아요.
items.passage: Have you heard about the Big Five? They are lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and buffaloes. You can see them all in Kruger National Park in South Africa.

items.q: 다음 중 관계대명사 which의 쓰임이 올바른 문장은?
choices: The bag which it is on the table is mine.
The bag what is on the table is mine.
The bag which is on the table is mine.
The bag who is on the table is mine.
The bag which are on the table is mine.
items.exp: 선행사가 사물(The bag)이므로 주격 관계대명사 which를 쓰고, 선행사가 단수라 동사는 is예요. 관계대명사 뒤에 주어 it을 또 쓰면 안 돼요.
items.passage: If you are lucky, you can see rhinos [which are sleeping] under baobab trees.

items.q:
윗글의 밑줄 친 부분처럼 조건을 나타내는 if절에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제로 쓴다. 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home.
choices: rained
raining
will rain
rain
rains
items.exp: 조건의 부사절에서는 미래를 현재시제로 나타내요. 주어 it이 3인칭 단수이므로 rains가 옳아요.
items.passage: [If you are lucky], you can see rhinos which are sleeping under baobab trees.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: The game was canceled because of the typhoon.
The game was canceled because the typhoon.
The game was canceled because of it was a typhoon.
The game was canceled because of the typhoon came.
The game was canceled because of the typhoon was coming.
items.exp: because of 뒤에는 명사(구)가, because 뒤에는 「주어 + 동사」가 와요. 나머지는 because 뒤에 명사만 있거나 because of 뒤에 절이 와요.
items.passage: However, the Big Five are in danger [because of] too much hunting.

items.q:
다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
I was late (A) the heavy traffic. I was late (B) the bus was stuck in traffic.
choices: (A) because - (B) because
(A) because of - (B) because of
(A) so - (B) because of
(A) because of - (B) because
(A) because - (B) because of
items.exp: (A) 뒤에는 명사구 the heavy traffic이 오므로 because of, (B) 뒤에는 절 the bus was stuck이 오므로 because예요.
items.passage: However, the Big Five are in danger because of too much hunting.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 사냥 감시에는 드론과 헬리콥터를 쓰지 않고 순찰대만 쓴다.
공원은 처음부터 사냥이 금지된 구역으로 유지되어 왔다.
자원봉사자들은 동물 덫을 설치하는 일을 한다.
Big Five가 위험에 처한 것은 먹이가 부족하기 때문이다.
공원 안의 야생동물은 울타리 안에서만 움직일 수 있다.
items.exp: 23번 문장에서 공원은 처음부터 사냥 금지 구역이었다고 했어요. 드론과 헬리콥터로 감시하고, 봉사자는 덫을 제거하며, 위험의 원인은 지나친 사냥이에요.
items.passage: Have you heard about the Big Five? They are lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and buffaloes. You can see them all in Kruger National Park in South Africa. Many wild animals move around this park freely. If you are lucky, you can see rhinos which are sleeping under baobab trees. However, the Big Five are in danger because of too much hunting. To protect the Big Five, the park has been a "no-hunting" area from the start. These days, drones and helicopters are used to monitor hunting activities. Also, the park runs many nature volunteer programs. Volunteers monitor signs of illegal hunting activities and remove animal traps.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 has been과 현재완료의 용법이 같은 것은?
choices: I have seen that movie three times.
She has lost her key, so she can't enter.
Have you ever been to Jeju?
She has lived in Busan for ten years.
He has just finished lunch.
items.exp: has been ~ from the start는 과거부터 지금까지 이어지는 상태이므로 계속 용법이에요. has lived ... for ten years도 계속이에요. 나머지는 경험, 완료, 결과, 경험이에요.
items.passage: To protect the Big Five, the park [has been] a "no-hunting" area from the start.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: I have visited Busan last summer.
She has played the violin since she was six.
We have known each other for five years.
Have you ever seen a flying squirrel?
He has just left the room.
items.exp: last summer처럼 명확한 과거 시점을 나타내는 말은 현재완료와 함께 쓸 수 없어요. I visited Busan last summer.가 되어야 해요.
items.passage: To protect the Big Five, the park has been a "no-hunting" area from the start.

items.q:
다음 문장을 수동태로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
Volunteers remove animal traps.
choices: Animal traps were removing by volunteers.
Animal traps are remove by volunteers.
Animal traps removed by volunteers.
Animal traps is removed by volunteers.
Animal traps are removed by volunteers.
items.exp: 수동태는 「be동사 + 과거분사 + by 행위자」예요. 주어가 복수이고 현재시제이므로 are removed가 옳아요.
items.passage: These days, drones and helicopters [are used] to monitor hunting activities.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: The windows were broken by the storm.
English is speaking in many countries.
The picture was painted by my uncle.
This song is loved by many teens.

items.passage: National parks are special places for preserving nature. The park is making efforts to preserve its natural beauty. First, it controls the number of visitors, so they should book to enter the park. Second, only some park trails are open to visitors for hiking. Third, the park makes visitors take their trash with them when they leave. There's one more thing: the hotels in the park do not use plastic and only use eco-friendly products. However, the Big Five are in danger because of too much hunting. To protect the Big Five, the park has been a "no-hunting" area from the start. These days, drones and helicopters are used to monitor hunting activities. Volunteers monitor signs of illegal hunting activities and remove animal traps. National parks preserve the Earth's past, present, and future. Thanks to them, future generations will also be able to experience many natural wonders.
